Always set the Content-Type header when sending JSON data. For example: ["Content-Type: application/json"]. Without it, servers like FastAPI may return 422 Unprocessable Entity.
Use JSON.stringify(data) to serialize your payload. Note: it returns null if you pass non-serializable objects (e.g., Nodes, RIDs).
The body parameter in request() must be a String, not a PackedByteArray. If you have binary data, encode it properly (e.g., base64).
For large downloads, consider using chunked processing to avoid memory issues.

cancel_request()
Cancels the current request.
request(url, custom_headers=[], method=HTTPClient.METHOD_GET, request_data="")
Starts an HTTP request.

url: The target URL (must include protocol, e.g., "https://...").
custom_headers: Array of strings like "Header-Name: value".
method: One of HTTPClient.METHOD_*. Default is GET.
request_data: Body for POST/PUT. Must be a String.

set_use_threads(use_thread)
If true, the request runs on a separate thread (default). Set to false for debugging.

request_completed(result, response_code, headers, body)
Emitted when the request finishes.

result: One of RESULT_SUCCESS, RESULT_CANT_CONNECT, etc.
response_code: HTTP status code (e.g., 200, 404, 422).
headers: Array of response headers.
body: Response body as PackedByteArray.

Troubleshooting
Why do I get 422 errors with FastAPI?
FastAPI requires explicit Content-Type: application/json for JSON endpoints. Godot does not set this by default. Always include it in your headers.
Why does JSON.stringify() return null?
You passed an object that contains non-serializable data (e.g., a Node reference). Only use basic types: int, float, String, Array, Dictionary.
How to test my endpoint?
Use Postman or curl first to verify your API works independently of Godot.
